name: inkjet
description: Rust batteries-included tree-sitter highlighting with bundled grammars and multiple formatters

host-language.comment: Rust crate. The bundled grammar parsers and scanners are C/C++ generated by tree-sitter and linked in at build time.

form-factor.comment: Library only. The repo has an examples/terminal_highlight.rs example, but there is no CLI binary.

license.comment: MIT OR Apache-2.0 according to the crate manifest; the repo ships LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE. Vendored grammars keep their upstream licences, and some vendored Helix themes include their own licence files (src/theme/vendored/licenses).

documentation.comment: There is no docs site. The documentation is the README plus the docs.rs API reference.

first-release.comment: 0.1.0 was published on crates.io on 2023-08-06. The GitHub repo was created the same day.

latest-version.comment: Checked 2026-11-19. Released 2024-09-15. There will be no further releases because the repo is archived. Master has two later commits (Markdown language, HTML-escape tweak) that were never released.

engine-model.comment: A thin wrapper around tree-sitter-highlight (re-exported). Each language gets a lazily built HighlightConfiguration from its tree-sitter parser plus highlights, injections and locals queries.

regex-engine.comment: The grammars are generated tree-sitter parsers, not regex rules.

embedded-languages.comment: Uses tree-sitter injections. The HTML injections.scm injects javascript into <script> and css into <style>. Highlighter resolves the injected language through Language::from_token, so the injected language's feature must be enabled (all-languages is on by default).

language-auto-detection.comment: The language is chosen explicitly from the Language enum or looked up by name token. There is no content-based guessing.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: Language::from_token maps names and aliases (e.g. 'rs', 'rust', 'hpp', 'mk') to a language. Many aliases happen to match file extensions, but there is no path, filename, shebang or MIME lookup API. Judged the same way as giallo's alias-only lookup.

resumable-line-state.comment: Every highlight call parses the whole source. There is no per-line state API.

incremental-reparsing.comment: All highlight_* methods call tree-sitter-highlight on the full source. No edit or old-tree API is exposed.

semantic-distinctions.comment: Highlights come from tree-sitter queries on the syntax tree, and locals queries are passed to HighlightConfiguration where a grammar provides them (e.g. Python, JavaScript, Ada). The Helix-derived highlight names distinguish e.g. variable.parameter, function.method and type.builtin.

bundled-languages.comment: Count of language-* feature flags in 0.11.1 (78), minus plaintext, which is a no-op. TypeScript/TSX, JavaScript/JSX and OCaml/OCaml interface are counted separately. Checked 2026-11-19. The README says 'over seventy'. Unreleased master adds Markdown.

grammar-format.comment: Vendored tree-sitter grammars (generated C parsers) with highlights/injections/locals .scm queries, many of them taken from Helix.

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Takes tree-sitter grammars that check in the generated parser and have a highlights.scm written for base tree-sitter. The README says extended nvim-treesitter queries will not work.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: Language::Runtime wraps a fn() -> &'static HighlightConfiguration, so a caller can supply any tree-sitter grammar and queries without forking. The grammar still has to be linked into the caller's binary.

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: All enabled grammars are linked into the executable at build time; languages are chosen only through Cargo features. Only the HighlightConfiguration (query compilation) is built on first use and cached in a LazyLock.

grammar-accuracy.comment: Upstream tree-sitter grammars with Helix queries, last refreshed for 0.11.0 (tree-sitter 0.23, September 2024). The issue tracker shows no frequent mis-highlighting reports, but nothing has been updated since then and the repo is archived, so grammars fall further behind upstream over time. Rated 3 for staleness, not for reported bugs.

bundled-themes.comment: 91 Helix themes vendored as constants in theme::vendored in 0.11.1 (e.g. Catppuccin Mocha, Dracula, GitHub dark/light, Gruvbox, Solarized, Tokyo Night). Checked 2026-11-19.

theme-format.comment: Theme::from_helix parses Helix TOML theme definitions at runtime. Themes can also be built in code, since Theme's styles/fg/bg fields are public. Since 0.11.0; before that there was a bespoke theme API.

token-classification.comment: A fixed list of tree-sitter capture names taken from Helix scopes (HIGHLIGHT_NAMES, e.g. 'function.macro', 'variable.parameter'). The Html formatter turns these into space-separated classes.

css-class-output.comment: The Html formatter emits <span class="keyword function">. ThemedHtml emits inline styles instead.

multi-theme-output.comment: The class-based Html output could be styled by any stylesheet, but no CSS themes or CSS-variable output are shipped. ThemedHtml inlines a single theme.

public-token-api.comment: Highlighter::highlight_raw is documented as an advanced method that returns the underlying tree-sitter-highlight HighlightEvent iterator.

ir-kinds.comment: HighlightEvent::{Source{start,end}, HighlightStart(Highlight), HighlightEnd}. Highlight indexes into constants::HIGHLIGHT_NAMES. The syntax tree is not exposed.

serializable-ir.comment: The events are tree-sitter-highlight's in-memory Rust enum, with no serde support. serde is used only to deserialize themes.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: No API returns tokens with styles already resolved. Callers can resolve a style themselves with Theme::get_style(HIGHLIGHT_NAMES[idx]), which is what the ThemedHtml and Terminal formatters do internally.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: HighlightEvent::Source carries byte offsets start and end into the source.

custom-formatter-api.comment: The public Formatter trait has write/start/finish hooks (plus io::Write variants). The README advertises it as 'pluggable formatters... writing your own is easy'.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: No line or range annotation mechanism. It would have to be built in a custom Formatter.

output-formats.comment: Html (classes) and ThemedHtml (inline styles) are on by default. The Terminal formatter needs the optional `terminal` feature; it writes 24-bit Color::Rgb through termcolor, which may downgrade on terminals without colour support.

line-numbers.comment: None of the bundled formatters emit line numbers.

streaming-output.comment: highlight_to_writer writes each event as it is produced, but it needs the complete source up front. The same reasoning as for tree-sitter-highlight and arborium.

terminal-ready.comment: The Terminal formatter (added in 0.11.0) needs the non-default `terminal` feature.

native-dependencies.comment: Compiles the tree-sitter C runtime (through the tree-sitter crate) plus the C/C++ parsers and scanners for every enabled language. The README mentions over 23 million lines of C and long build times.

runs-in-browser.comment: No browser build, npm package or documentation for it.

wasm-build.comment: No official WASM artifact and no documented wasm32 support.

synchronous-api.comment: All highlight_* methods are synchronous. They take &mut self, so parallel highlighting needs one Highlighter per thread.

bindings-ports.comment: No current bindings. Historically, the Elixir library Autumn wrapped inkjet in a Rust NIF up to v0.2 (its README credits 'Inkjet for the Rust implementation up to v0.2'). It later moved to its own crate, autumnus.

core-package-size.comment: crate_size of the inkjet 0.11.1 .crate on crates.io (about 24.5 MB, compressed source with all vendored grammars). The size of the compiled binary depends on which language features are enabled.

throughput-tier.comment: No independent or reproducible comparative benchmark found.

initialization-cost.comment: Not measured. The docs warn that the first use of a language builds its HighlightConfiguration, 'a non-trivial operation' with noticeable latency, which is then cached.

monthly-downloads.comment: crates.io recent_downloads (90 days) of 93,380 divided by 3, checked 2026-11-19.

maintenance-status.comment: The repo was archived on 2025-09-04. The README says 'Inkjet is no longer supported by me' and recommends autumnus (by Leandro Pereira, a past inkjet contributor) as the successor. The Elixir wrapper Autumn has since been renamed lumis.

documentation-quality.comment: Solid README (features, language table, Cargo features, FAQ) plus a docs.rs API reference with examples. No docs site or guides.

notable-users.value: Autumn (Elixir, up to v0.2); supercat; gazetta-render-ext
notable-users.comment: crates.io lists 7 reverse dependencies, all small. Autumn (now renamed lumis) used inkjet as its Rust backend through v0.2.

bus-factor.comment: Personal repo of Colonial-Dev (57 of 69 commits). leandrocp made 9 commits; three others made one each. Now archived.
